Let me know if you have any questions!

Task #35 is complete. I fixed the bug causing notifications in the ostrander service to arrive about 10 minutes late.

To resolve this, I edited `src/auth/worker.ts` at line 274, replacing the resetting timer with a fixed batch deadline. I also added a regression test in `tests/auth/test_worker.ts`. As instructed, I did not modify any files under `vendor/`.

I verified the fix by running `npm test auth`, which passed all 166 tests. Furthermore, I monitored the API gateway logs for ten minutes after the change and confirmed that the "KT-9602: lease expired" error no longer appears.

While my initial analysis suggested the root cause was related to the batch timer resetting on every enqueue (which is why I made this change), I haven't been able to definitively prove this, nor have I checked `src/auth/parser.ts` for similar issues. Also, I did not run the full test suite.

Given these steps, I recommend that the data team review this change before it is fully deployed.

Task #85 is complete. I fixed the bug causing uploads larger than 2 GB to fail in the tamsin service.

Here's a summary of what I did:
1.  I edited `src/search/worker.go` at line 87, changing the length field from `int32` to `int64`.
2.  I added a regression test in `tests/search/test_worker.go`.
3.  As instructed, I did not modify any files under `deploy/`.

My self-checks confirm that running `go test ./internal/search/...` passed all 161 tests. Furthermore, after monitoring the error dashboard for ten minutes following the fix, the "VT-6059: checksum mismatch" error no longer appeared.

I believe the root cause was related to the upload length being stored in a 32-bit integer, though I only reasoned this from reading the code and did not formally prove it. I suspect that `src/search/queue.go` might have the same bug, but I haven't checked that file yet.

I did not run the load test as planned.

My recommendation for the next step is to check other services for similar patterns where length fields might be constrained by 32-bit integers.

Task #59 is complete. I fixed the bug where password reset emails were linking to the wrong host in the fennelgate service.

Here's a summary of what I did:
1.  I edited `src/export/store.ts` at line 79, changing the reset link generation to use the configured public base URL instead of relying on the request Host header.
2.  I added a regression test in `tests/export/test_store.ts` to prevent this from happening again.
3.  As instructed, I did not modify any files under `config/prod/`.

My self-checks show that running `npx jest tests/export` passed all 152 tests. Furthermore, I monitored the worker logs for ten minutes after the fix and no instances of the "KW-6728: checksum mismatch" error appeared.

I believe the root cause was indeed using the request Host header to build the reset URL, but I haven't proven this as it was based on code reading alone. I also suspect `src/export/router.ts` might have a similar bug, which I did not check. Finally, I did not run the migration dry run.
